newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crudes firm after Brent trades higher.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crudes firm after Brent trades higher.

text.p: North Sea physical premiums were firm on Tuesday in line with a stronger Dated Brent trade, although the Brent paper market eased lower.
A wet Brent cargo loading Dec 21-23 traded at Jan Brent +33 cents, the buyer the Wall Street trader that already holds some five Brent cargoes, traders said.
Dated Brent last traded on Monday at just Jan Brent +22.5 cents for a Dec 20-22 loader.
Differentials for other North Sea grades were talked steady, with few cargoes left unsold for December.
Jan Brent paper was trading some 43 cents down at $23.67 a barrel at 1650 GMT in line with the IPE screen.
Intermonth spreads eased from Monday with Jan/Feb talked around +55/+58 and Feb/March at +60/+62.
A cfd for next week was traded at Jan Brent -5 cents, after a Dec 23-27 cfd changed hands at Feb Brent +40 cents.
Traders said that Dated Brent's rebound looked fairly secure given an open transatlantic arbitrage.
"The U.S. is tight and there's certainly a potential to sell cargoes," said one trader.
The buyer of today's Brent cargo was believed to be working at least one VLCC to the U.S.
Other North Sea grades were talked unchanged from Monday, a Norwegian producer said.
Statfjord was sold out for December, while three or four Osebergs, one Ekofisk and one Draugen remained, he said.
In the Mediterranean, two Urals cargoes, loading Dec 10-15, were traded on Monday on a private and confidential basis, with the discount to Dated Brent pegged around 15/20 cents.
